description: D-CORE, the Database of Chinese Overseas Renewable Energy Projects, is a project-level dataset by the International Institute of Green Finance at the Central University of Finance and Economics, with the Institute of Development Studies, deposited on Harvard Dataverse. It tracks renewable energy projects outside mainland China that involve Chinese enterprises as developers, EPC contractors, equipment suppliers, investors or financiers. Each record gives host country and sub-national location, technology (solar PV, wind, hydropower, energy storage, geothermal, biomass and integrated systems), installed capacity, the developer and the Chinese entities including whether they are central state-owned enterprises, project stage and milestone timeline, and financing. The page says it is compiled from public news and corporate disclosures with an AI-assisted extraction pipeline with deduplication and normalisation, and covers more than 1,400 projects with data to June 2026. The events table and a data dictionary are free under CC BY-NC 4.0; the deposit is to be updated quarterly and was last updated in July 2026. Coverage is global outside mainland China, from 2022. Caveats: news-derived records may miss or mis-state projects, and commercial use is barred. Simulation uses are pipeline and planned capacity for generation expansion scenarios in host countries. Related records: data-gem-global-gas-infrastructure-tracker is another project-level tracker.
